draft.title: Access to services
card: Services are things a community needs, such as hospitals, schools and shops. Most are found in cities, where many people live close together.
Smaller and remote places have fewer services, because there are fewer people to use them. People there often travel a long way to reach a hospital, a high school or a large shop.
Travel can take a lot of time and money. It can also make it harder to get help quickly, for example in a medical emergency.
Liveability is how good a place is to live in. Easy access to services can make a place more liveable, and long trips to reach them can make it less so.
draft.remember: Services gather where many people live, so people far from cities often travel further for them.

a.q: Why do remote places often have fewer services than cities?
opts: Fewer people live there to use the services
The services there are too cheap to run
People in remote places do not need services
Cities have more land for the services
a.why: Services are usually built where many people can use them, so they cluster in cities. Remote places have fewer people, so they have fewer services. People there still need services, which is why they travel.
a.clue: Think about how many people live in each kind of place.

b.q: Tom's family lives on a remote farm in the Northern Territory. The nearest hospital is a long drive away. How does this most affect the liveability of his home?
opts: Reaching medical help takes longer and is harder
Tom's family has more services close by
Tom's family has no need of medical help
The farm is easier to reach from the city
b.why: A long trip to a hospital makes it harder to get help quickly, which lowers liveability. Having services close by is the opposite of Tom's case. Families in remote places still need medical care.
b.clue: Think about what a long drive means in an emergency.

a.best: Fewer people live there to use the services

b.best: Reaching medical help takes longer and is harder
